notes.title: Hotfix 1.05
notes.content: [p][i]Hey. Hey why didn't you all tell me the demo was nigh-unplayable. Hey. Hey guys. Hey guys why didn't you tell me the demo was borked.[/i][/p][p]Sorry about that, y'all! You all SHOULD be able to get through the demo's full contents now, both on Steam and itchio. Additionally, for the full game's version 1.05:[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a few typos here and there through the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Made one specific CG unlock in the gallery, regardless of which path you achieve it on.[/p][/*][*][p]Actually re-added another CG to the gallery! No clue how that one got missed, but you all [i]should[/i] max out at 257.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks a bunch for being patient with me! We actually blew through my lifetime sale goal a few days ago, and we're almost at 10 reviews! I cannot tell you all how much I appreciate it, haha.[/p]

notes.title: Hotfix 1.04
notes.content: [p]Hi y'all! This one's pretty small, but it should be nice for anyone who's run into some snags.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Fixed a path in Chapter 6 that accidentally skipped a scene and triggered Chapter 7 early. (This one really hurt; the scene it skipped over is one of my personal favorites.)[/p][/*][*][p]Added some visual static in Chapters 3 and 4 that wasn't working previously. Nothing major, and you can always get rid of it with the Screen Filter option if it hurts your eyes![/p][/*][*][p]Made the screen sway on the train in Chapter 3. Same as the filters, you can disable that with the Extra Animations option if needed, but it's still nice to have.[/p][/*][*][p]GREATLY reduced the file-size of updates!! No more redownloading 400+ MB of music and art every time an update gets pushed out; your updates [i]should[/i] be around the 20-50 KB range now. That's the update size I've consistently gotten, anyway; yours may vary a little, but it should never breach an MB now.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a nice little Easter egg for people who've gotten all 6 endings. If you've already gotten them at the time of this update, you [i]should[/i] be able to see it just by launching the game![/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks for your support and for being patient with me! Hopefully, no major updates will be needed at this point, but bug-fixes will be way less taxing on you all.[/p][p]-Trinket[/p][p]P.S. If you haven't picked up VLT yet, now would still be a great time to do so! The launch day sale will keep the game 10% off for another 6 days as of this writing - you've got until July 24th to save a few bucks on this tale of rage and rot![/p]

notes.title: Hotfix 1.03
notes.content: [p]Hi y'all! Another day, another hotfix. Just minor stuff this time, nothing that's gamebreaking like 1.0.2.[/p][list][*][p]Re-synced some sprite-expression movement in Chapter 6.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some issues with full-screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Unblurred the screen where it wasn't intended with Ending 4. (Some parts of the CG [i]are[/i] meant to be blurred for effect, but not to the extent it previously was. Ending 3 is intentionally meant to blur, though!)[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some spacing issues with the full content warning system.[/p][/*][*][p]Actually made a few chunks of achievements unlockable in the second half of the game. (No idea how that one happened, but it should generally be okay now!)[/p][/*][*][p]Cleaned up some typos here and there.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks for being so patient with me! I think I've gotten everything that was pointed out, but if you noticed something else, don't be afraid to tell me on the Discussion Board! Every little bit helps![/p]

notes.title: Hotfix 1.02
notes.content: [p]Fixed a bug that prevented 3/6 endings from occurring. Sorry about that, guys! Hopefully, it should be back to normal (it's everything in the non-Obsession version of Chapter 8; if you can progress past the choices in Ch8 on a normal route, you SHOULD be okay!).[/p][p]I'm still collecting info on any minor glitches and visual errors that may have slipped by me, so please feel free to list them in the discussion board if/when you see them! Every little bit helps![/p]

notes.title: Delaying the Game's Launch Date
notes.content:
[i]Well this is kind of embarrassing.[/i]

This is not the post I wanted to make. I wanted to be counting down the days until the game drops, not explaining why the Valentine's Day release might not be possible.

I've been in the middle of moving houses since early November. I've mentioned this once or twice on my BlueSky, but it's taken a lot more out of me than I expected. Long story short, I've been going back and forth between the two houses for 1-2 weeks at a time, and my current setup in the new place isn't optimal. Add that in with everything that comes with moving house on top of game dev, and it's kind of been a recipe for disaster regarding my release date.

When I first put VLT up on Steam back in June, I set the release date for what I thought was [i]more[/i] than enough time to finish the writing, programming, CGs, and polish everything to my own standards. I've always been kind of picky about the visual novels I read - if VLT isn't something that I would gush over to my friends with minimal complaints, why am I subjecting the broader Steam audience to it?

This was before I realized "hey, wow, Chapters 3-5 are really lacking in meat and need to be expanded." This is before I realized the presentation for the chapters was kind of dull, and needed some punching up. And, of course, this was before we knew we'd be closing on the new house. The game's scope has expanded for the better since June, but so has my workload and real life situation.

Right now, in its current state, Veins Like Tapeworms has:

[list]
[*] Almost 100,000 words in total
[*] 150+ CGs at least sketched, if not fully rendered
[*] 6 endings going full speed ahead
[*] 5+ Bonus Scenes
[/list]

...and so on and so forth. I never thought it'd get to be this in-depth, but I wouldn't change it for the world. It's just that, until further notice, I won't be able to get substantial work on the game done for at least half my time.

All this to say: I'm tentatively setting Veins Like Tapeworms' new release date to [b]March 17th, 2025.[/b] It's not as thematically appropriate as the yearly day of love, but you'll probably need a stiff drink after some of the darker endings. I'm not going to make any promises and say [i]this is definitely happening and no setbacks can stop me,[/i] but March the 17th is the new day I'm aiming for.

Thanks for sticking with me over the months. We actually hit my wishlist goal on January 15th; I couldn't be more grateful to all of you who stumbled across my first "big" visual novel and saw enough potential to put it on your wishlist.

Sorry for the delay. I hope you all understand why I'm doing this. I don't want to ship a half-baked product just to meet a goal, and if the shoe was on the other foot I'd rather wait a little longer for a perfect product.

notes.title: Participating in the RPG Maker Horror Festival!
notes.content:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39252092/sale/RPGMakerHorrorFestival]Come check me out at the RPG Maker Horror festival![/url]

Did you know [i]Veins Like Tapeworms[/i] is built in RPGMaker MZ? It's not something that most people can pick out from a glance!

I love RPGMaker; I wouldn't be here on Steam, presenting VLT to you all, without it. That's why I'm overjoyed to tell you all that Veins Like Tapeworms is officially part of Gotcha Gotcha Games' first ever RPG Maker Horror Festival! This is a great time to try out VLT if you've been eyeballing it for a while! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45112129/f920a4115f2d349faf5b35049a49a372881581f2.png[/img]

A two-chapter demo is already available, so you can get a nice taste of what's to come in the story. You can even leave a review on the demo's page! As of this writing, VLT's demo has 10 reviews already! It's one of the best ways to support the game right now.

And hey, if nothing else, just clicking that Wishlist button is free, takes 5 seconds, and really helps support a one-woman band!

Anyway, I know I've been a bit radio-silent on Steam regarding VLT's progress, but I'd say it's plugging along really nicely! Here's a little snapshot of the game's progress so far:

[list]
[*] [b]65,000+ words[/b] implemented so far!
[*] Almost [b]all 8 chapters[/b] fully sprited!
[*] [b]All 6 endings[/b] written and implemented!
[*] At least [b]100 different illustrations[/b] - whether that's sketched, lined, or fully rendered in the game! 
[*] [b]4 out of 7 Bonus Scenes[/b] fully written!
[/list]
I'd probably say VLT's in a completely readable state. It's not 100% done just yet - there's still a lot of illustrations to do and a bit of cleaning up with the writing - but play-testers can boot up the game right now, read it from beginning to end, and get a complete vision of the story.

And, as proof, here's a few screencaps of brand new stuff I've been working on:

I've been a busy little bee!

notes.title: Demo now available!
notes.content:
Hey all! After a few days of getting tied up in Steam appeals, I'm happy to announce that you can now play the first two chapters of [i]Veins Like Tapeworms[/i] for free! Players will be able to experience:

[list]
[*] 2 chapters
[*] 1 ending
[*] 1 Bonus Scene
[*] 13,000~ words
[*] 45+ images to unlock
[/list]

I'm working on getting a Mac version up and running as we speak! It's just giving me a [i]tiny[/i] bit of a headache, since I'm a Windows user, but with any luck Mac players should be able to read it in the next week or so! For any Windows users who enjoyed the demo, please be sure to wishlist the full game on Steam - every one of you count, and are super appreciated!

But that's all for now. Won't you take a moment to enjoy the beginning of a monstrous descent?
